prompt:
I need the front end for Sondewell. Configuration software for the instrumented monitoring buoys and shore stations at a university limnology field station, used to set how each sensor samples, flags and reports data through the seasons.

Who's using it: Mareike Holt, the station's data manager and only full-time technician. She has run the buoy network for six years, knows every sensor's quirks, and writes the QA rules herself. Faculty and graduate students depend on the data feed but don't change settings.

What they're doing right now: Ice is forecast to form on Lake Tamarack within ten days, so the main buoy has to come out and the under-ice moorings switch to their winter profile. Mareike is copying last winter's profile into this season, setting the dissolved-oxygen sondes to sample every 30 minutes instead of every 10, turning off the chlorophyll sensor that freezes, raising the low-battery cutoff for the cold, and changing the spike-detection threshold on the thermistor chain because last winter it flagged real mixing events as errors. A graduate student has also asked for the under-ice station to report conductivity in µS/cm instead of mS/cm for her thesis, and Mareike has to decide whether to change it station-wide or only in that student's export. Nothing should take effect before the buoy retrieval date she sets.

What's in the system at this point: Four deployments: Main Buoy (pulled for winter on Dec 2), Under-Ice Mooring North (14 m depth), Under-Ice Mooring South (9 m), and Shore Met Station. 31 sensors in total, each with model, serial number, calibration date (two DO sondes overdue, last calibrated Apr 18), current sampling interval, units, and active/inactive state. Three saved profiles: Open Water 2026, Winter 2025–26, Storm Mode. QA rules per variable: range limits (water temp −0.5 to 30 °C), rate-of-change limits (thermistor 1.5 °C per 10 min), flag codes. Battery and telemetry settings: 12.1 V cutoff, satellite uplink every 6 h in winter. Change history covering 212 edits since 2021, each with author and reason. Five data consumers subscribed to exports, each with their own unit preferences.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
